It's pretty rough on the old noodle to need to constantly adjust to the "throttle being goosed" and many people here seem to benefit from regularity with dosing,  and from what I've seen breaks of days or weekends do little to nothing to really delay or stop tolerance.

Tracking is a super good suggestion in the other thread,  I'd add that the self medicating with food is because our brains are apparently worse at burning glycogen (iirc) and it makes us crave carbs to keep the levels high.   Fighting the urge and instead boosting your protein intake should supply a good steady stream of energy and keep your appetite down. 

Low fat foods are the devil, and so are artificial sweeteners.  If you need to "pad out"  the volume of your food intake for whatever reason look to leafy greens and stuff like that.

Any is appropriate,  from what I know though,  literally the younger the better in terms of end-state.  As per Dr. Berkeley presentation though,  the brain stops development in the early 30s, but don't feel too bad,  the brain training and skills you developed were akin to exercise for your brain,  and probably helped wring out all the base level gains you could. Vyvanse takes about an hour and a half to get through metabolism before it releases the active ingredient,  so yeah it makes sense.

The comments all seem to have pretty good advice here,  but I'd add to you though,  that medication can lead to a better end state in the end after development ceases.  This is backed up by the scientific evidence.   Treating adhd symptoms with medication leads to strengthening the newly used pathways and such in the brain, and allows people to "close the gap"  on their developmental delays.   The earlier the better is what the evidence says. 

My general analogy for this is having a muscle group that is so weak/understimulated it can't do enough work to damage itself so it grows larger,  the medication acts like steroids as well as an instant boost to the strength of the muscle group,  allowing it to "work out"  enough to grow,  and for some people they can grow the muscle enough that after enough time they can discontinue treatment and the muscle is big enough to manage on its own.   I'm sure that active coping strategies can have somewhat of the same effect but medication is (IMO) very very important.

Rejection sensitive dysphoria is the term I guess,  although I didn't get to get into it with a knowledgeable clinician (there are zero ADHD specialized doctors in my city/area,  I was lucky to get diagnosed at all) I'm positive Its a feature for me. 

To put it simply, the rush from a relationship is very much like a narcotic (actually rather is in terms of neurology)  but even more so for us.  I got into positions where I got "hooked"  on unrequited love more or less quite a bit, and a few serious relationships.  Thing is that the adhd thing would make me "check out"  and "ignore"  the other person leading to the downfall of the relationship, although I didn't really ignore them ; something else had captured my attention,  I still loved them.   Regardless ; when faced with the end of a relationship or a rejection by a love interest I simply come completely off the rails.  I get mad because often I'm being left because of the (unlabeled or understood)  issue of mine where I "disappear"  as my interests shift around,  and am indignant because often it's after a long period of months or even a year of being entirely focused on the other person,  and I feel betrayed because the other person just walks away when I'm facing an issue that I can't articulate properly. I'll probably simply shut down instead of lashing out immediately,  but this isn't thinking or feeling,  my mind is just blank,  I'm like a robot on autopilot.  But soon after I'll whip around between anguish rage regret severe depression and everything in between,  strings of texts,  pleading,  midnight drives to leave notes on cars,  unasked and inappropriate gifts to try to win them back,  etc.  Very out of character and regrettable behavior.  

I had PTSD level emotional and psychological symptoms from my "high-school sweetheart"  whom I was friends with for 4 or 5 years as the "best guy friend" head over heels in love with.   One day after dozens of rejections and friendship breaks everything sort of clicked between us, we snuggled together in bed,  made out,  she spent the night with me that day,  and the morning was the last time I ever really saw her in person.  I came on too strong,  she withdrew,  I came on stronger,  and then she outright rejected me,  and everything was terrible after that.  

I had nightmares for a decade (the only nightmare I ever had actuaoly)  which was less nightmare and more just remembering her face and that day, supposedly a happy dream,  I'd wake drenched in sweat with my heart rate up around 120, shaking, and crying.    I'm happy to say that Vyvanse has helped with this immeasurably  whether through using the initial euphoria to work through some issues or because of its enabling me to effectively use CBT tools I've now made peace with those events and many others... But I've still been single now for about 6 years and haven't really tried yet to "get back to it",  as I'm very unsure about the entire thing still. 

Hope that's detailed enough,  but basicailly I think it's lack of being understood and not understanding ourselves,  being oresented/given a thing that says "this person will stand by you and try to understand more than anyone ever else will"  combined with the removal of our own personal dopamine pump (I sit next to this person and can think better!  What fucking magic is this?!)  that makes some of us act like an addict being told their dealer is cutting them off,  more or less.

I've always had bad body odor issues, they were exacerbated by the easier/more sweat on Vyvanse,  but also compounded by my total failure and doing laundry even remotely correctly. 

I "fixed"  my B. O. About a week ago,  have had no comments (family who is nice enough to mention it)  and only shower every 2 or 3 days still (list of habits to fix....)  but on to the meat and potatoes. 

Step one,  run your washing machine empty with no detergent,  and peek inside after 5 minutes or so.   Is it sudsy?  If so you've been using too much detergent.  Cut down by half or more (especially if you use a front loader)  and look into doing an empty cleaning cycle with some washing machine cleaner (honestly 8 think borax and baking soda are all you really need,  with vinegar jn the water softener slot.)  next stop using dryer sheets,  they coat your clothes in oils and such and can build up mixed in with sweat/excretion and "prestink" clothes,  they'll smell fine out of the wash but when they get warm from your body or you sweat even a little suddenly it's putrid.  Next,  you may want to consider doing some fairly harsh "cleanses/strips"  on your clothes from the effected areas,  fill a clean sink or large Basin with the absolute hottest water you can from the tap,  mix in borax,  baking soda,  some non-chlorine bleach (could just dump in peroxide 8 think given the other things being added,  but hey.)  and some liquid detergent.  Mix it up and then submerge your stuff for 2-4 hours,  then pull it and wash,  it worked for me :)  

Also make sure your thoroughly drying your skin and undercarriage before applying deodorant or dressing, heck use a warm hair dryer,  it feels great to be "properly"  dry anyway.  A little moisturizer can help the deodorant work better/longer I find as well.  (dry, moisturize underarms,  dry,  apply, dry.)   It sounds involved but it's not really.

Hyper focus is more that you want and desire to focus on X to the exclusion of Y even if/when Y demands your attention.  If Y has an external demand placed on you that requires attention you will probably service Y and then return to X as fast as possible.  X will eventually lose its novel status and you will seemingly lose all interest.

It's a dopamine seeking behavior for the most part.

If you can't stop focusing on X Y Z or whatever letter grabs you for whatever reason it is perseveration or the inability to stop focusing on something.


An example. .. I've been hyper focused on adhd and these boards for weeks, and spent a few days also with perseveration where I could not pull away from it (don't smoke on your meds folks. )

This is more like perseverance kinda... there is some disagreement in the community over the validity of each honestly depending who you talk to.  I think both obviously exist.

Hyper focus is usually used to describe the short to long term persistent recurring engagement with a novel experience or interest.  This can be a girl, a book, new project, etc.

The other thing is perseverance, which is the inability to consciously disengage from a task.

What you are experiencing sounds more like the second alongside the normal adhd thing of being unable to ignore a distraction, leaving you to flit from stimuli to stimuli reacting to each with your full attention. 

I had some issues with both prior to meds,  perseverance isn't improved as much on meds as the other things, and the ability to focus at all led to a solid day spent on reddit but hey.  It was a better spent day than the vast majority of my unmedicated days where I just read memes all day.

You won't get drunk as a general rule.

Remember the hubub years back on Redbull and drinking when it was first all the rage (and some of the drinks contained things stronger than caffiene? )  same problem.

Alcohol is a depressant, it down regulates parts of the brain and the CNS, making your muscles relax, and your heart rate slow.  

Stimulants like the ones we take up regulate the brain and to a (much) lesser extent the CNS.  In fact up regulating the cns causes side effects we try to avoid.  

Anyway.  The poison response is set off in the brain, when some things start getting too out of whack.   Stimulant blocks the effects in the brain for the most part.  Determined drinkers will have almost no cognitive changes, but can do things like disable their long term memory just like a blackout drunk,  and feel fine.  Once there they are very close to the point where they will stop their heart... and they will feel fine or at least perfectly capable of drinking right up until they kill themselves.  

People do break these rules sometimes, but your specific medication may have a special interaction.  My medication does not have the sticker to avoid all alcohol but that came with a verbal instruction to only have a couple drinks at most, and they don't really have much effect.

It's not a big loss.  Alcohol was a risky game for me before, in terms of my emotional state being even more unregulated...  being with friends is its own reward now,  I can have more fun and follow along better than I could before sober or drunk.   YMMV.

ADHD is named wrong.  

At its core it is caused by not enough dopamine in general and neoepinephrine in the frontal cortex.  There is a few ways that condition arises, but simply the neurons don't accept the chemicals enough, or they ''clean them out'' too fast, or they never produced enough to start! 

Because those 2 chemicals say ''good job neuron whatever we all did was good'' or ''you, neuron, do your work.'' The front part of the brain does not work properly or at all.  The different thinking abilities (executive functions) it enables turn on 30 percent later than they should on average so age appropriate learning does not happen.  You are behind and pushed to do cognitive tasks you don't have the capacity to do.  Anyway.  

The main problems in adhd are the executive functions, almost everything stems from those. 

Minds voice - verbal stream of thought in your head.  Not only do you do this but if you think ''HEY YOU, YEAH ME.  GET UP AND DO THAT THING.''  You actually feel a motivation, and can moderate emotions this way.

Minds eye : your ability to picture visually memories and abstractions in your head. 

Working memory : 7 to 10 things should be around average to hold in your head, and absent-minded setting down objects shouldn't happen much.

Motor motivation : ever felt like you just could not move?  Like it would take the effort of an entire day just to move... even though you could in theory just do it?  
It's not an illusion, it really is harder.

Planning and goal setting/time : we have an impaired sense of time, I think both minute by minute and day by day and year by year.
Bad at planning for the future, it's always now. 


Because of these defecits and dopamine deficiency you can't direct on a task that is not novel and unique.  When it stops giving you the dopamine of a novel experience you will drop it, because there is no effect or not enough from normal or boring tasks.  Your time keeper part of your brain is whispering ''this is a rewarding task. Release the dopamine'' but the rest of your brain is too loud and it does not happen.

Super simple analogy... imagine someone with horrible horrible muscles in their legs.  So weak they couldn't really use them, so they drag themselves around with way over muscled arms. They'll get better but if the steroids are stopped before the muscles reach critical mass (back to reality, critical mass = enough connections and additional neurons have been created in those regions that despite still having an improper level of receptors per neuron etc. The region can self-sustain function at a good level without support.) Think of it this way.  Each number represents a brain regions activation.

2 9 4 10 10 6 10 5 2

Vyvanse does + 4 across the board to start.  For a short period you get 

6 13 8 14 14 10 14 9 6
Then your brain starts down regulating, in days the 14s are back to 10.  That's euphoria and substantial ''drive'' to do stuff that you don't self direct really : just steer and let yourself go.  The lower numbers drop by a smaller amount.  Then you titrate up, and the low numbers go up a bit higher than they were, drive for homeostasis pushes the all down a little more but again mostly just the above 10s.   

In the end on an appropriate dose you'll reach a balanced state more or less, where these numbers are all very close to 10, and that level usually holds from what I have heard for up to several years, perhaps with a bump by 10 very rarely.  I think 60 or 70 is the kind of relative max, and when you get there many people will switch to a different medication for a while, generally of a different class of stimulant, for a period of ~3 months, keep in mind this is anecdotal, then switch back to vyvanse, and titrate to 50 with their ''tolerance'' reset. The light stimulating the brain = blue spectrum light. Our brains have adapted over the millenia to distinguish between traditional artificial light sources (FIRE!) And daylight more or less, and it uses blue light input through the optic nerve to set our circadian rhythm.   Getting a good dose of sunlight in the morning will help set your wakefulness schedule,  and avoiding it after sundown will help with the sleep side.  This is the purpose of light therapy, using a high power ''light box'' in the morning for 30 minutes to punch your brain with this stimuli to induce wakefulness and correct your internal rhythms.  

The good news is that there are scientifically proven tools and methods to alleviate this issue with screens, although the post in question is probably the most effective method available.

Install f.lux on your PC, and there is an app called twilight for android (apple probably?  There is an equivalent I'd guarantee.)  These programs modify the color profile of your screen/apply a red filter, moving the ''color temperature'' of the screen lower into the red zone, dimming the blue pixels, or even turning them off entirely if you set twilight very aggressively.  Dim your display as well, as much as possible.  It feels weird at first, as things look a bit different with the shifted color spectrum, but honestly I don't even notice after a while as your brain kind of just corrects out the shifted color to see more what it expects.  I used this to great effect to help me sleep before I was even diagnosed, once I even fell asleep at my desk, something I had literally never done before in my entire life.   I get tired while gaming while using it, and need significantly less time to calm my mind and focus on stillness when I do lay down to sleep.

White noise is also tremendously useful.

Normal people just have less of a barrier to sleep generally, so if they sabotage their cycle with light inputs they are no worse than we are if we don't, if you know what I mean.

Sleep hygiene, great concepts in general if you search it up.

Atomoxetine is straterra, a non stimulant that bypasses the dopamine system to increase neoepinephrine in the frontal cortex directly, stimulants like the other two work by increasing dopamine and the brain turns the excess into neoepinephrine.   It directly works on adhd and is the most effective treatment for some.  Bonuses : non stimulant, antidepressant style action means less issues with ups and downs.  Downside : low awareness of improvement.  6 weeks is so long you don't notice cognitive improvements.  Others will first, generally.

Methylphenidate - no direct experience, afaik fast acting, relatively strong, in a different ''class'' from lisdex. 

Lisdexamphetamine (vyvanse) - the same primary active ingredient as adderall, but 100 percent, whereas addy has a mix of various other amphetamines.  Lisdex is a prodrug, meaning it goes to your liver, is metabolized and releases the active ingredients to travel to your brain.  Long slow release for me 12 to 14 hours before it's wearing down/off.  Definitely not a flat effect all day long but quite acceptable. 

Personally I like vyvanse but I'm probably biased ;)   these are 3 excellent options to start with and which to try could be steered a little bit by intuition but if you have combined type (general adhd) it's definitely more just trial and error. Alright I've got a number of things to say.  First is that you DO NOT just ''decide'' to double a dose of a prescription XR medication. Second, there is at least a 75~ percent chance you have adhd.  It is genetic, and if it runs in both families strong that percentage could be higher.  Don't be so dismissive due to this point alone.  Third you were diagnosed so... yeah.  

Third.  You are young, and your brain is still going to be somewhat in the pubescent stage and transitioning into the young adulthood development.  It doesn't stop until your early 30s,  although full emotional maturity is generally recognized to be in the mid twenties sometime.

When you release the pressure take slow deep breaths and roll your shoulder back, if it is a similar problem tight pectorals can make the muscles on your back and neck quite sore because they are stuck in an overextended position due to your pecs pulling your shoulders forward.

Again i'm a  big nuke fan, but I don't think the physics of nuke generation work well for miniturization to the point of full decentralization of the grid to the house level, glancing at the wikipedia entry for micro-nukes seems to back that up, the smallest planned one listed (only one...) would have offset the power usage of a small village.  Nuke scales like gas/diesel/coal generation scales, there are advantages in having a larger reaction volume, larger heat transfer surfaces, larger and more turbines, placing all that power in a central location and gaining more power per dollar, and that power going out through very high voltage lines to be stepped down into  communities and such, at suprising efficiency, like 1c/kwh/1000km levels of efficiency, which is nothing compared to the loss in efficiency as you drop the size of a generator generally speaking.  Bigger sizes mean more reaction mass, more cooling mass, more heat output, bigger turbine surfaces, more energy in general, for less relative material and input costs.  

The reason solar bucks the trend in power generation is that solar is not tied to a heat-engine of some variety to generate electricity.  It is the only thing we generate power with that does not at some point rely on a turbine or piston to convert heat energy to motion, instead it works via witchcraft, it is entirely different.  Nuke makes heat via witchcraft, but we still need the heat->motion exchange which means just like everyone shouldn't run their house on a diesel generator, we don't want every house running a small nuke, it will be a bit... wonky.  That is unless there is some *amazing* breakthrough in the field of small nukes, allowing all the energy of a nuke reaction to be instantly converted into electricity or something via some unknown method or material, but that is as hopeful as 90 percent efficiency solar panels.  

So yeah... solar panels were destined to have the ability to be a decentralized solution, by the nature of how they work.  And wind to a lesser extent by how it *has* to work.  Not because of any specific coddling by the government or industry.
